# Switch between projects on a map

Choose a project to replace the loaded model and move the map to its location in the same viewer.

## How it works

<h3>Try it</h3><ol><li>Zürich district opens with the map enabled. Choose Rotterdam bridge to replace it and move to the Netherlands.</li><li>Choose Zürich district to switch back. Only the selected project's model is loaded.</li><li>Open View at the top right → Layers and choose Street or Satellite.</li><li>Select a component, then click 1 element selected at the top left to open Properties.</li></ol>
<h2>Developer integration</h2><p>Create one <code>Viewer</code> and await <code>viewer.ready</code>. For each project change, await <code>viewer.clear()</code>, download the selected IFC, await <code>viewer.add()</code>, then await <code>viewer.toggleMap(true)</code>. Clearing releases the previous project's models and geographic context; enabling the map after import uses the new project's coordinates. The host never disables the map between projects or creates another viewer. Project controls are disabled during the transition to prevent overlapping imports. Download, import and map errors use the SDK message API; choose either project to retry.</p>
<h3>Geographic placement</h3><p>Both complete IFC files are imported unchanged and have native map conversions. Zürich uses Swiss LV95 (EPSG:2056) and LN02 heights, including model terrain. Rotterdam's Van Brienenoord bridge uses Amersfoort / RD New (EPSG:28992). The bridge source does not declare a vertical datum; this example retains its original heights and does not claim survey-grade terrain alignment. The SDK owns map layers, attribution and geographic placement.</p>
<p>Copy this folder and serve it over HTTP, for example <code>python -m http.server 8080</code>. Open <code>http://localhost:8080/</code>; the SDK, models and map tiles require internet access.</p>

<h2>Rotterdam bridge</h2><p>Geonovum GeoBIM georeferencing practice dataset and original model authors. W3C Software and Document license as published in the source repository. <a href="https://github.com/Geonovum/GeoBIM_Georefereren/blob/0fe0f5e89676de3d21fc3219eb5805b36e29e032/data/voorbeeldmodellen_Infra/Van%20Brienenoordbrug-IFC4X3.ifc" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Original IFC at the pinned revision</a>. <a href="https://github.com/Geonovum/GeoBIM_Georefereren/blob/0fe0f5e89676de3d21fc3219eb5805b36e29e032/LICENSE" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">W3C Software and Document license</a>. The IFC bytes are unchanged. The source's projected CRS does not declare a vertical datum; no terrain height correction is applied. The publisher reports a small XYZ offset against AHN. This is geographic context, not a certified survey overlay. <a href="https://github.com/Geonovum/GeoBIM_Georefereren/blob/0fe0f5e89676de3d21fc3219eb5805b36e29e032/09%20Praktijktoets%20georefereren.md" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Publisher's placement validation</a>.</p>
<p>Complete original published IFC4 urban geodata export; contents unchanged. Buildings, terrain and mapped infrastructure use Swiss LV95 (EPSG:2056), metre units and the declared LN02 height datum. The model includes its own IFC terrain; the optional 30 m Copernicus surface includes roofs and vegetation. This is geographic context data, not a detailed construction-design model.</p>
